relevance_note: Patient #15 of this 15-child cohort carries a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant ("1 TNFAIP3 mutation (A20 haploinsufficiency, #15 with BD)"), inherited from his affected mother.
method_note: Worked from the Markdown only. A Python script (in my scratch dir) split the Table 1 and Table 2 rows on "|" and built every table-row span as the row prefix from the patient label through the cell, so table spans are verbatim by construction; I chose every feature, status and mapping by reading the rows and text, and checked the script output against the tables. Scope: all 15 enrolled patients (Table 1, rule 6) are included, although only #15 carries a TNFAIP3 variant; the other 14 can be filtered out via the variants table. Relatives named in the "Familial history" column and in the text are their own rows (rule 5); the paper has no family labels, so I built labels on the paper's own pattern "the patient #15 mother" (e.g. "patient #3 aunt", "patient #15 grandmother"). The mother of #15 is a TNFAIP3 carrier (Table 2 STATUS (carrier) "HZ(mother)"; text "also carrying the A20 mutation") with BD; the grandmother is affected (BD, complaints similar to #15) but her carrier status is not reported. Table 1 ages are in years (column headers "Age at enrollment (y)" and "Onset (y)"); age at enrollment is recorded as age at last evaluation, though #15 was followed up for at least 6 months more (age not given). ISO durations use decimal years where needed (P0.3Y). Age at diagnosis is not reported. Transcripts come from Methods (unversioned, e.g. TNFAIP3 NM_001270508), which the Table 2 legend says the variant column refers to. Variant types are not described in words, so "not reported". The TNFAIP3 variant has only in-silico support (GERP 5.63, CADD 39, LRT D, MT D; SIFT and PP2 na); there is no functional assay, so functional evidence is "not reported". dbSNP IDs and the cytoband (6q23.3) are not captured. "De novo" for #1 and #10 comes from Table 2 STATUS (carrier) plus the Methods statement on Sanger testing of parents "when available". is_proband is true only for #1, #2, #10 and #15, the patients for whom Table 2 shows parental carrier status ("validated ... both in proband and parents"); null for the other enrolled patients. Not recorded as features: HLA B51 (a genetic marker), "Familial history: no", and for #15 "usually normal CRP" (not an unqualified absence). Pathergy "–" is recorded as excluded using the legend ("-": negative result; the table uses an en dash). The IFN score counts as increased above 2.466; the six positives match the text (#1, #8, #9, #10, #12, #15). Checklist judgments: #15 GI marked observed from "perianal ulcerations" plus "Fecal calprotectin ↑" (uncertain). #15 recurrent fever observed from "Fever" plus "no further recurrence of ... fever crisis". #13 "fever" is not stated as recurrent, so not reported. Narrower or unqualified findings were not promoted: #1 hemolytic anemia was not called autoimmune, so cytopenia (autoimmune) is not reported; #10 "Hepatitis" was not called autoimmune, so autoimmune hepatitis is not reported; #10 recurrent paronychia and oral candidiasis are not marked as recurrent infections; #12 HSP and #1 mother GPA are not marked vasculitis because the paper does not call them that; #8 ANA- does not exclude autoantibodies. Skin lesions observed for pustulosis, folliculitis, erythema nodosum, skin ulcers, skin abscesses, lichen vulvar and chilblains. Contradictions in the paper: (1) #1 is "F" in Table 1 (12 females, consistent with the abstract) but the text says "he carried the p.N574T variant"; sex recorded as female. (2) The #5 DNASE1L3 protein change is "T971fs*2" in Table 1 but "p.T97Ifs*2" in Table 2; Table 2 used. (3) For #1, Table 1 says "Stimulated STAT1 ↑" but the text says no clear increase in STAT1 expression; both quoted in functional evidence. (4) The Discussion assigns "mycophenolate mofetil and colchicine in the first case and ... hydroxychloroquine in the second one" in an order that conflicts with Table 1 (#1 HCQ, #10 MMF+colchicine); treatments follow Table 1 and the Results. (5) The Discussion says all pathogenic carriers had onset "before the age of 6 years", but #10 onset is 6. (6) The text calls the #15 grandmother's grandson "the nephew"; quoted verbatim. No contradictory phenotype statements, so no checklist items were neutralised for contradiction.
